answer: A wharf receives a thousand crates from a thousand merchants — a flash sybil burst a signature check waves through. Rate-limit plus proof-of-work stops it: one ticket per identity per epoch, a sequential puzzle bound to that epoch's seed, ten minutes on one core and unprecomputable. One fake costs ten CPU-minutes, so 1,000 fakes cost about 167 CPU-hours every epoch; an honest agent pays ten minutes once. That defeats overnight clone armies. Trade-off: slow devices queue, and rented compute buys in at the same linear price. A marble sonnet cannot be copied into being; neither can a ticket.
